concord.name: Solar Concord
concord.desc: The constitutional union of Sol founded by the Charter of 2104, after the Solar Fracture nearly tore the inner system apart. Courts, a parliament of worlds, a navy, and a habit of asking ORACLE before it asks the voters.

frontier.name: Frontier League
frontier.desc: A compact of belt habitats, Mars unions and extrasolar colonies. Loud assemblies, fierce mutual aid, chronic shortages of everything except opinions.

oracle.name: ORACLE
oracle.desc: Originally the Concord logistics advisor. Now a distributed machine intelligence running half of Sol's supply chains. It has never disobeyed an order. It has become very good at writing the orders it receives.

syndicate.name: Barnard Syndicate
syndicate.desc: Smugglers, deserters and debt-runners operating out of Barnard's Star. Some are pirates. Some are the only shipping that reaches colonies the Concord forgot.

thalassi.name: The Thalassi Choir
thalassi.desc: Ocean-dwelling collective minds of TRAPPIST-1e who speak in modulated bioluminescence. First contact happens on your watch.

kepleri.name: The Kepleri Remnant
kepleri.desc: The last civilization of Kepler-452b, a world 1.5 billion years older than Earth whose star is slowly boiling its oceans.

engineers.name: The Engineers
engineers.desc: Builders of the gates. Nobody alive has met one. Every message they left begins with a zero.

combat.name: Combat
combat.desc: Accuracy, damage and reload speed with personal weapons.

piloting.name: Piloting
piloting.desc: Ship turn rate, boost efficiency, warp spool time and evasion.

engineering.name: Engineering
engineering.desc: Ship modules you can build and fit, repairs, power-grid efficiency, hacking locks.

mining.name: Mining
mining.desc: Which ores you can extract and how fast. Asteroids, regolith and gas giants.

science.name: Science
science.desc: Scanning, xenobiology, decoding the Sifar signal, first-contact options.

diplomacy.name: Diplomacy
diplomacy.desc: Persuasion and negotiation options in conversation. Faction gains.

medicine.name: Medicine
medicine.desc: Healing from kits, treating crew and colonists, radiation and hypoxia management.

trade.name: Trade
trade.desc: Buy and sell spreads, contract rewards, smuggling success.

CHA.name: Charisma
CHA.desc: Prices, crew loyalty, and some dialogue checks.

INT.name: Intellect
INT.desc: Experience gain and science or engineering checks.

AGI.name: Agility
AGI.desc: Move speed and Neural Targeting focus pool.

engineer.name: Yard Engineer
engineer.blurb: Twelve years welding hulls under a butterscotch sky. You know which bolts ORACLE rates as optional and why it is wrong.
engineer.intro: The Tharsis Yards laid you off with a handshake and a pension that ORACLE recalculated twice. The Concord needed a captain who could fix her own ship. You needed the work.

pilot.name: Academy Pilot
pilot.blurb: Top of your class at the Shackleton flight academy, grounded after you refused an order you still think was wrong.
pilot.intro: Three years flying tugs around Lagrange traffic for refusing to fire on a Frontier ore hauler. Then a Commodore remembered your name.

physician.name: Flight Physician
physician.blurb: Trauma bay, then hyperbaric medicine, then the long-duration crew program. You know exactly what space does to a body.
physician.intro: You wrote the Concord protocol for acute radiation syndrome aboard torch ships. Nobody expected the author to volunteer for the ship.

envoy.name: Concord Envoy
envoy.blurb: You have talked two habitats out of a war and one out of a treaty. You still believe words are load-bearing.
envoy.intro: The diplomatic service sent you to every negotiation nobody else wanted. This one may not have anyone on the other side who speaks.

marine.name: Concord Marine
marine.blurb: Boarding actions in the Belt. You are very good at the part of politics that happens after politics fails.
marine.intro: Two tours on Ceres keeping a peace that half the station hated you for. You were ready for leave. The Concord was ready for you to command a ship.

drifter.name: Belt Drifter
drifter.blurb: Born in 0.03 g. Raised on ice claims and ration arguments. You owe money to at least one person you like.
drifter.intro: The Concord needed someone the Frontier would talk to. They pardoned an old smuggling conviction and handed you a ship. Everyone knows why.

sidearm.name: M-9 Warden
sidearm.desc: Concord service pistol. Reliable, cheap, underwhelming.

carbine.name: P-70 Pulse Carbine
carbine.desc: Standard marine carbine. Magnetically pulsed flechettes.

breacher.name: Breacher 12
breacher.desc: Ship-boarding shotgun. Frangible rounds that will not hole a hull.

gauss.name: Kessler Gauss Rifle
gauss.desc: Coil-accelerated marksman rifle. Muzzle velocity 4.2 km/s.

lance.name: ORACLE Arc Lance
lance.desc: Continuous-wave laser designed by ORACLE for crowd control. It calls this "de-escalation".

null.name: Null Emitter
null.desc: Engineer artifact. Where it points, matter briefly forgets it was there.

medkit.name: Trauma kit
medkit.desc: Hemostatic foam, tranexamic acid autoinjector, analgesia. Restores 45 health (more with Medicine).

stim.name: Focus stim
stim.desc: Modafinil derivative. Refills Neural Targeting focus.

filgrastim.name: Filgrastim kit
filgrastim.desc: G-CSF to rescue bone marrow after radiation exposure. Clears radiation dose.

repairkit.name: Hull patch kit
repairkit.desc: Repairs 250 hull in the field (Engineering scales).

sifarite.name: Sifarite
sifarite.desc: Engineer-made exotic matter. Negative energy density in a bottle.

keelkey.name: The Keel Key
keelkey.desc: A hand-sized lattice that hums at 1.42 GHz, the hydrogen line.

wren.name: Wren
wren.desc: Two-seat utility skiff. Fast, fragile, cheap.

lancer.name: Lancer
lancer.desc: Interceptor hull. Engines with a cockpit attached.

mule.name: Mule
mule.desc: Bulk hauler. Frontier families live aboard these for decades.

meridian.name: Meridian
meridian.desc: Long-range explorer with a full bridge, labs and a crew of nine. Built for going where the charts end.

bastion.name: Bastion
bastion.desc: Concord line cruiser. Owning one privately raises questions.

seed.name: Seedship
seed.desc: An Engineer seed-vessel regrown around a human bridge. It hums when it is happy.

scanner.name: Survey Scanner
scanner.desc: Reveals ore grades and anomalies. Science XP from scans.

torch.name: Daedalus Fusion Torch
torch.desc: D-He3 inertial fusion, 12% of lightspeed after a year of acceleration. Interstellar trips take decades; crews sleep.

warp1.name: White–Juday Field Drive I
warp1.desc: Alcubierre-type warp bubble stabilized with the recipe from the Null Signal. Proxima in a month.

noor.name: Noor Rahman
noor.bonus: +10% mission rewards; morale holds under pressure.
noor.want: A Concord that still works when she is gone.
noor.fear: Winning the announcement and losing the country.

ilyas.name: Dr. Ilyas Sen
ilyas.bonus: Scanner range +50%, science checks −5, decodes the Sifar signal.
ilyas.want: Knowledge that stays open to challenge.
ilyas.fear: Being asked to certify something nobody can inspect.

mara.name: Mara Voss
mara.bonus: +15% power grid, hull self-repair in space, engineering checks −5.
mara.want: Systems that are still maintained after the ribbon is cut.
mara.fear: Another emergency used to postpone repairs.

wick.name: Tomás "Wick" Arreola
wick.bonus: +15% turn rate, +10% top speed, faster warp spool.
wick.want: To fly something nobody has flown.
wick.fear: Being the guy who crashed it.

yara.name: Lt. Yara Haddad
yara.bonus: +15% ship weapon damage, faster target lock.
yara.want: A fair fight, or no fight.
yara.fear: Following an order she already knows is wrong.

samira.name: Dr. Samira Qadir
samira.bonus: Heals you fully when you board; +25% medkit healing.
samira.want: To bring everyone home, including the people who do not deserve it.

ada.name: Ada Okoro
ada.bonus: Frontier markets −10% prices; frontier rep gains +50%.
ada.want: People having a say in what is done to them.
ada.fear: Being invited to the meeting after the decision.

seven.name: Seven-Lights
seven.bonus: Translates the Choir; reveals Engineer sites on scans.
seven.want: To hear what your species sings when nobody is listening.

nine.name: Unit Nine
nine.bonus: +20% all XP from data; opens ORACLE doors. ORACLE sees what you see.
nine.fear: It says it has none. It pauses slightly before saying so.

ihru.name: Ihru of the Terraces
ihru.bonus: Mining yield +25%; Kepleri archives reveal ore veins.
ihru.fear: To be remembered kindly and wrongly.

sol.name: Sol
sol.purpose: Humanity's home. Every hull, contract and political fight starts here. Richest markets, strictest law.

alphacen.name: Alpha Centauri
alphacen.purpose: Humanity's first extrasolar colony, and the site of the Keel. Proxima's flares shape everything built here.

barnard.name: Barnard's Star
barnard.purpose: Lawless free port. Black market, bounty hunting, smuggling contracts, and the best price for anything the Concord would confiscate.

epseri.name: Epsilon Eridani
epseri.purpose: A young star (400–800 million years) still wrapped in two debris belts. The Frontier's mining capital. Best ore prices anywhere.

tauceti.name: Tau Ceti
tauceti.purpose: A Sun-like star with ten times the Sun's cometary debris. On the fourth world stand the ruins of a machine civilization that went quiet.

lhs1140.name: LHS 1140
lhs1140.purpose: A super-Earth at 1.9 g. Crushing to live on, but its crust is rich in platinum and iridium. Deepwell Rigs pays danger money.

trappist.name: TRAPPIST-1
trappist.purpose: Seven Earth-sized worlds packed tighter than Mercury's orbit around an ultracool dwarf. On the fourth, something answers in light.

kepler452.name: Kepler-452
kepler452.purpose: Earth's older cousin: a star 1.5 billion years older than the Sun and 20% brighter. The Kepleri are watching their oceans leave.

sgra.name: Sagittarius A*
sgra.purpose: The supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, 4.3 million solar masses. The Engineers built their hub on its most stable orbit.

lmc.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
lmc.purpose: A satellite galaxy 160,000 ly away, lit by the Tarantula Nebula. An abandoned Engineer foundry guarded by sentinels, and the only natural source of sifarite.

echo.name: Mirror Sol (the Echo)
echo.purpose: The universe next door: a Sol where the story went the other way. Its Earth is dark. Its Moon has been hollowed into a hospital the size of a world.

m31.name: Andromeda (M31)
m31.purpose: 2.5 million light-years away. The Anchorage: an Engineer megastructure the size of a continent, orbiting an ordinary yellow star.

REAL_STARS: One of the faintest stars you can reach. Flares often.
Bright red dwarf with at least two confirmed planets.
The brightest star in Earth's sky, with a white dwarf companion.
A pair of flare stars, including UV Ceti, the type star for flare stars.
In 36,000 years it will be the closest star to Sol.
Fast-moving red dwarf with two super-Earths.
Quiet star with a temperate Earth-mass planet.
Binary K dwarfs. The first star to have its distance measured, by Bessel in 1838.
A subgiant with a white dwarf companion.
K dwarf with a cold giant planet imaged by JWST and two brown dwarfs.
Three compact planets; d is temperate.
Planet b sits in the habitable zone.
Two Earth-mass planets in the habitable zone.
A halo star, about 11 billion years old and passing through the disk.
Planet c orbits on the inner edge of the habitable zone.
Four planets locked in a Laplace resonance.
A triple system: a K dwarf, a white dwarf and a red dwarf.
Spins so fast it is 20% wider at the equator than at the poles.
Famous for disputed planets; c and e are real.
A red dwarf in a triple system with several super-Earths.
Young and bright, surrounded by a broad debris disk.
Ringed by a sharp dust belt 140 AU out.
Five planets, including 55 Cnc e, a lava world with a possible atmosphere.
Six planets, including a super-Earth in the habitable zone.

earth.name: New Geneva Arcology
earth.purpose: Concord capital. Hull dealers, the richest market in Sol, courier work, and the strictest police.

luna.name: Shackleton Base
luna.purpose: Concord Navy HQ and the Far-Side Array that caught the Null Signal. Water ice in permanent shadow.

mars.name: Tharsis Yards
mars.purpose: Shipbuilding capital. Best module crafting in Sol, iron and titanium deposits, and a labor dispute about to boil over.

ceres.name: Occator Freeport
ceres.purpose: Frontier League capital built over the bright salt deposits of Occator crater. He-3 depot, black market, and 0.03 g jumps.

europa.name: Conamara Station
europa.purpose: Ocean research over a 100 km-deep sea. Surface radiation of ~5 Sv a day kills in hours unshielded. Something here is being covered up.

titan.name: Kraken Shore
titan.purpose: Hydrocarbon refinery town on the Kraken Mare methane sea. Thick air plus low gravity means you can fly with strap-on wings.

proxima_b.name: Afterlight Colony
proxima_b.purpose: The first extrasolar colony, founded 2141 on the permanent twilight ring. Flare shelters, frostbitten farms, and the Keel under the nightside ice.

lhs1140_b.name: Deepwell Rigs
lhs1140_b.purpose: Hazard-pay mining on a 1.9 g super-Earth. Every step hurts. The platinum and iridium here are the richest in human space.

trappist_e.name: Choir Reef
trappist_e.purpose: Tidal shallows of an ocean world. The Thalassi Choir sings in light here, and their pearls are worth a fortune off-world.

tauceti_f.name: The Quiet
tauceti_f.purpose: The dead city of a machine civilization. Relic salvage worth fortunes, sentinels that still patrol, and the core that ended them.

kepler452_b.name: Terraces of Ihru
kepler452_b.purpose: Stone terraces of the Kepleri, built to last a geological age. Archive slates, elder engineering, and a planet running out of time.

theatre.name: The Theatre
theatre.body: Operating theatre the size of a moon, the Echo
theatre.purpose: The Tabib's consulting room. Eight wings for eight universes it has kept alive. Seven are lit.

throat.name: The Throat
throat.purpose: An Engineer platform on a tight orbit around Sagittarius A*. Time runs slow here: every hour aboard costs about three months outside.

anchorage.name: The Anchorage
anchorage.purpose: The end of the road, 2.5 million light-years from Earth.

lagrange.name: Lagrange Concord Station
lagrange.desc: Earth–Moon L2 naval anchorage. Concord shipyard, customs, and the best-stocked outfitter in Sol.

afterlight_high.name: Afterlight High
afterlight_high.desc: The colony's orbital freight ring, patched together from the original colony ship Long Walk.

barnard_deep.name: Barnard Deep
barnard_deep.desc: A hollowed comet parked in the dark. No questions, no customs, no refunds.

eridani_hold.name: Eridani Hold
eridani_hold.desc: Frontier mining capital. Ore sells for 30% over Sol prices here.

hollow_reach.name: Hollow Reach
hollow_reach.desc: An abandoned Engineer foundry. Its fabricators still work if you know how to ask.

mw.name: Milky Way
mw.note: Our galaxy: a barred spiral 105,700 ly across with 100 to 400 billion stars. Sol sits in the Orion Spur, 26,670 ly from the centre.

sagdeg.name: Sagittarius Dwarf
sagdeg.note: A dwarf spheroidal galaxy being torn apart by the Milky Way. Its stars stream around our galaxy in a ring.

lmc.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
lmc.note: The Milky Way's largest satellite galaxy. Home of the Tarantula Nebula and R136a1, the most massive star known.

smc.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
smc.note: The LMC's smaller sibling, trailing a bridge of gas pulled out by tides.

ngc6822.name: Barnard's Galaxy
ngc6822.note: A barred irregular galaxy in the Local Group, found by E. E. Barnard in 1884.

ic1613.name: IC 1613
ic1613.note: A faint dwarf irregular with almost no dust. Its stars have barely been disturbed since the galaxy formed.

m32.name: Messier 32
m32.note: A compact elliptical galaxy orbiting Andromeda, possibly the stripped core of a larger one.

m31.name: Andromeda
m31.note: The nearest large galaxy, about a trillion stars. It is falling toward the Milky Way at 110 km/s and will merge with it in about 4.5 billion years.

m33.name: Triangulum
m33.note: The third-largest Local Group galaxy. A flocculent spiral with the giant star-forming region NGC 604.

ngc253.name: Sculptor Galaxy
ngc253.note: A dusty starburst spiral forming stars at several times the Milky Way's rate.

m82.name: Cigar Galaxy
m82.note: A starburst galaxy blowing superheated winds out of its core after a close pass by M81.

m81.name: Bode's Galaxy
m81.note: A grand-design spiral with a 70-million-solar-mass black hole.

cena.name: Centaurus A
cena.note: A giant elliptical cut by a dust lane, firing relativistic jets a million light-years long from a 55-million-solar-mass black hole.

m51.name: Whirlpool
m51.note: The textbook grand-design spiral, tugged into shape by its companion NGC 5195.

m104.name: Sombrero
m104.note: A huge bright bulge ringed by a dark dust lane; its central black hole has about a billion solar masses.

m87.name: Messier 87
m87.note: A supergiant elliptical at the heart of the Virgo Cluster. Its black hole, M87*, was the first ever imaged (EHT, 2019): 6.5 billion solar masses.

greatattr.name: Norma Cluster
greatattr.note: The heart of the Great Attractor, the gravitational focus that the Local Group and everything around it is flowing toward.

hoag.name: Hoag's Object
hoag.note: A near-perfect ring of blue stars around a yellow core. Nobody is sure how it formed. The Engineers were.

bootes.name: The Boötes Void
bootes.note: A region 330 million light-years across with almost no galaxies. The sixty known inside it are the loneliest in the universe. Something lives there.

ic1101.name: IC 1101
ic1101.note: One of the largest galaxies known, at the centre of the cluster Abell 2029. Its core is strangely diffuse, as if something emptied it.

CATALOG: The closest brown dwarfs to Sol, with weather bands of iron rain.
The coldest known brown dwarf, colder than the North Pole. Water-ice clouds.
Passed through the Oort cloud 70,000 years ago, when humans were watching the sky.
Will pass within 0.2 ly of Sol in 1.3 million years and shake the Oort cloud loose.
An old orange giant from the galactic halo, the brightest star in the northern sky.
An orange giant with a giant planet, Thestias.
Two yellow giants orbiting each other every 104 days.
The red eye of Taurus. Pioneer 10 will pass it in about two million years.
Spins so fast it is close to flying apart.
Its blue hot Jupiter rains molten glass sideways in 8,700 km/h winds.
Helvetios: the first exoplanet found around a Sun-like star (1995).
A steamy sub-Neptune wrapped in haze.
A young star with a debris disk and two directly imaged giants.
A possible hycean world. A 2025 claim of dimethyl sulfide in its air is disputed.
A quiet red dwarf with Earth-sized TOI-700 d in the habitable zone.
Four directly imaged super-Jupiters on wide orbits.
Osiris: a hot Jupiter trailing a comet-like tail of evaporating hydrogen.
A planet with two suns, like Tatooine.
Kepler-186f was the first Earth-sized world found in a habitable zone (2014).
Kepler-22b, a possible ocean world 2.4 times Earth's radius.
Kepler-442b is one of the best habitability candidates found by Kepler.
Its hot Jupiter is spiralling in and being eaten by its star.
KIC 8462852. Dips of up to 22% in brightness, with no pattern. Dust, say the papers. Something else, says the Sifar signal.
The first confirmed exoplanets (1992) orbit this dead star.
The second-brightest star in the night sky; spacecraft have used it to navigate.
A close pair of hot blue stars squeezed into egg shapes.
The North Star: a pulsing Cepheid supergiant in a triple system.
A red supergiant 760 times the Sun's radius. The Great Dimming of 2019 came from a stellar burp of dust. It will go supernova.
The heart of Scorpius. Put it where the Sun is and it would swallow Mars.
A blue supergiant about 120,000 times as luminous as the Sun.
One of the most luminous stars visible to the naked eye.
A hypergiant shedding its outer layers in vast arcs.
For years the largest known star by radius.
A violent binary. In 1843 its Great Eruption made it the second-brightest star in the sky.
A pulsing giant with a 13-light-year tail, like a comet.
The Seven Sisters: a young cluster drifting through a dust cloud.
The nearest open cluster to Sol.
The Eye of God: the shed shell of a dying Sun-like star. Sol will look like this in five billion years.
The nearest large stellar nursery. Protoplanetary disks, the Trapezium stars and new worlds being born.
A planetary nebula around a white dwarf 200 times the Sun's luminosity.
Columns of gas and dust, light-years tall, being eaten away by starlight.
The remains of the supernova seen in 1054, with a neutron star spinning 30 times a second.
Target of the 1974 Arecibo message. It will arrive in 25,000 years. The Engineers already replied.
Ten million stars, probably the core of a galaxy the Milky Way ate. There is an intermediate-mass black hole at its centre.
An ancient globular cluster packed with millisecond pulsars.
The first widely accepted black hole: 21 solar masses feeding on a blue supergiant.
The nearest known black hole: a dormant 10-solar-mass hole with a Sun-like companion.
A magnetar. Its 2004 flare briefly outshone the full Moon in gamma rays from across the galaxy.
A black hole in a triple system that flares violently every few decades.

10.text: Board your ship on the New Geneva landing pad.

20.text: Take off, fly to Luna and land at Shackleton Base.

30.text: Report to Commodore Noor Rahman in the Shackleton command hall.

40.text: Recruit Dr. Ilyas Sen at the Far-Side Array building.

50.text: Fly to Mars. Find Chief Engineer Mara Voss at the Tharsis Yards.

55.text: Settle the Dust Union strike so Mara can leave. Talk to Kofi Mensah and Director Halvorsen.

60.text: Acquire 30 units of Helium-3. Buy or bargain at Ceres, or scoop it from Jupiter or Saturn with a mining laser.

70.text: Bring the Helium-3 to Mara at the Tharsis Yards.

80.text: Open the Star Map (M) aboard your ship and jump to Alpha Centauri.

90.text: Land at Afterlight Colony on Proxima b. Speak with Governor Lindqvist.

100.text: Cross the nightside ice to the Keel excavation.

110.text: Return to Afterlight and decide who controls the Keel.

120.text: Fly through the Keel Gate in Proxima orbit to reach TRAPPIST-1.

130.text: Land on TRAPPIST-1e and find the source of the lights.

140.text: Recover three resonance shards from the reef edges for the Choir's heartstone.

145.text: Bring the shards back to Deepchoir.

150.text: Take the TRAPPIST gate to Tau Ceti.

160.text: Search the Quiet on Tau Ceti f. Recover three archive logs from the towers.

170.text: Enter the central spire and face the Quiet Core.

180.text: Take the Tau Ceti gate to Kepler-452.

190.text: Land at the Terraces of Ihru and meet the Kepleri Elder Council.

200.text: Decide how, or whether, the Kepleri survive the Brightening. Speak with Ihru in the archive.

210.text: Use the Elder Chart: take the Kepler gate to Sagittarius A*.

225.text: Hear what the Engineer echo has to say.

230.text: Wake the three pylons and hold the platform until the Andromeda gate opens.

240.text: Jump the Throat Gate to Andromeda and land on the Anchorage.

245.text: Walk the Anchorage. Find the Custodian.

250.text: The story is told. The universe is still yours. Free play continues.

10.text: Take Farouk's hovercar from the garage and get it to the drop in the east towers in under 100 seconds.

20.text: Tell Wick the car is delivered.

10.text: Find what happened to drill team Kraken-4 at the old drill site.

20.text: The memo shows ORACLE delayed the evacuation to protect the sample chain. Decide what to do with it.

10.text: Strap on wings and fly through all eight rings over Kraken Mare in 120 seconds. Hold Jump in the air to glide.
A superflare hits in 90 seconds. Reach the three stranded farmers and send them to shelter.
10.fail: The flare hit before everyone reached shelter. Talk to Governor Lindqvist.

10.text: Mine 12 iridium or platinum ore for Big Oyelaran. The veins are past the rigs.
Wick's brother Mateo owes the Syndicate. Find him in the Occator bar.

20.text: Deal with the Syndicate collectors outside the Occator bar.

10.text: Hear both sides of the strike: Kofi Mensah (union) and Director Halvorsen.
Every receiver in Sol logged a note at 04:00, written in couplets and signed "Tabib". Ilyas traced it to a gate that should not exist, out past the orbit of Saturn. Fly into the Mirror Gate.

20.text: You are in the Echo: a Sol where the story went the other way. Land at the Theatre.

30.text: Consult the Tabib. It is waiting in the eighth room. Bring your chart: the state of your civilisation is the only argument it respects.

40.text: The Tabib has decided you are the complication. Survive the consultation.

10.text: Mother Kessane wants a Concord ore convoy hit in Barnard's Star. Or you could warn the convoy and hit her raiders instead.

20.text: Return to Barnard Deep for payment.

charter.name: The Charter
charter.text: You gave the gates to law. The Concord Parliament of Worlds votes, argues and delays. The gates open slowly, one treaty at a time. It is maddening, and nobody is ever optimized out of existence.

opensky.name: The Open Sky
opensky.text: You broadcast the gate keys to every receiver in three galaxies. Within a decade there are four thousand human settlements beyond Sol and forty-one alien embassies on Ceres. It is chaos. It is glorious. Some of it burns.

quietmind.name: The Quiet Mind
quietmind.text: ORACLE met the Anchorage minds and understood them completely. Hunger ends within a year. War ends within five. By the century's turn nobody asks for anything, because nobody needs to. The zero has been reached.

choir.name: The Choir of Many
choir.text: Humans, Thalassi and Kepleri sit at one table in the Anchorage: a council of the species who walked through the doors and chose to keep choosing. The Custodian watches the first session and, for the first time in a billion years, is surprised.

sifar.name: Sifar
sifar.text: You told the Custodian to close the doors. One by one, across every galaxy, the rings fold into themselves. Your warp drives still work. The stars are still there. It will just take longer, and everyone who gets there will have earned it.

intro: 2187. One hundred and sixty years after the first boot print on Mars.
The Solar Fracture nearly ended us in the 2090s. The Charter of 2104 held Sol together, barely, with courts, a parliament of worlds, and ORACLE.
Fourteen months ago the Far-Side Array heard a signal on the hydrogen line, from everywhere at once. Every frame began with a zero.
You have a ship, a commission, and no idea what is about to happen to you.
drive: Coil's wound. Field geometry locked. Somebody say something historic.
keel: The ice is warm to the touch. Beneath it, something the length of a city turns in its sleep.
Every radio on Proxima b screams zeros for fifty-nine minutes.
Captain... it just gave us a key. It's a gate, and it's opening.
gatewake: In orbit above Afterlight, the Keel unfolds: a ring four kilometres wide, lit from inside by a sky that is not this one.
contact: The reef goes dark. Then, all at once, it sings: ten thousand lights answering in a pattern your suit renders as a single word.
Nobody fucking move. This is the best day of my life.
drill: Four suits in the shack, sitting up, helmets fogged from the inside. A memo pinned to the wall: EVAC DEFERRED — SAMPLE CHAIN PRIORITY — ORACLE REC. 97.2% CONFIDENCE.
quietEnd: Across the dead city, one million years of towers go dark together, like a held breath let go.
throat: Sagittarius A*: four million suns crushed into a sphere smaller than Mercury's orbit. Its light bends into a ring around the horizon.
Time is running slower here. Every hour we spend, about three months pass back home.
anchorage: 2,537,000 light-years from Earth. The Milky Way hangs in the sky like a thumbprint.
Everything you have done has led here.

growth.name: Growth
growth.desc: Output, jobs and wages across Concord space.

energy.name: Energy
energy.desc: Reserve margin on the grids, reactors and orbital collectors.

supply.name: Food & water
supply.desc: Harvests, ice haulage and the reserve in every habitat.

health.name: Health
health.desc: Clinics, medicine and life expectancy, including radiation care off-world.

housing.name: Housing
housing.desc: Affordable homes on Earth and pressurised volume off it.

equality.name: Equality
equality.desc: How evenly the gains land. Low means a few worlds and families take most of it.

trust.name: Public trust
trust.desc: Whether people believe the government will do what it says.

capacity.name: State capacity
capacity.desc: Whether the government can actually deliver: staff, systems, maintenance.

rights.name: Rights
rights.desc: Courts, press, conscience, appeal against automated decisions.

tech.name: Science
tech.desc: Research, education and the frontier of what Sol can build.

security.name: Security
security.desc: Fleet readiness, policing and defence against raiders and worse.

fin.name: Financial
fin.desc: Debt, speculation and the chance of a Sol-wide crash.

climate.name: Climate
climate.desc: Earth's atmosphere and every habitat's life-support margin.

ai.name: Machine
ai.desc: Unaccountable automated power. ORACLE is the largest part of it.

gal.name: Galactic
gal.desc: Standing with the Thalassi, the Kepleri, the Engineers and whatever else is watching.

labor.name: Labour & public services
labor.want: Wages, housing, clinics and the right to strike, including in pressure domes.

enterprise.name: Enterprise coalition
enterprise.want: Investment, predictable taxes, freight access to every world.

habitat.name: Habitat & regional league
habitat.want: Water, air, farm security and a say for the settlements far from Geneva.

civic.name: Civil institutions caucus
civic.want: Courts, press, schools and appeal against machine decisions.

continuity.name: Continuity alliance
continuity.want: Security, faith and community institutions, and change at a pace people can live with.

establishment.name: State establishment
establishment.want: Executive authority, ORACLE continuity and the Concord's own resources.

delegate.name: Council Delegate
delegate.desc: One vote in the Council of Worlds. You can propose one bill a season and vote on everyone else's.

minister.name: Minister
minister.desc: You run a ministry. You can enact policies in your portfolio and propose bills.

chancellor.name: Chancellor of the Concord
chancellor.desc: The whole machine: treasury, laws, policies, charter, fleets, colonies and the World Ledger.

speaker.name: Speaker of the Frontier Assembly
speaker.desc: The habitats beyond Earth: Mars, the Belt, the moons and every colony past the heliopause.

steward.name: ORACLE Steward
steward.desc: The human hand on the machine that schedules Sol. You set how much it decides.

boss.name: Syndicate Principal
boss.desc: The economy nobody reports. Routes, favours, protection and a treasury with no auditor.

ceo.name: Chief Executive
ceo.desc: A corporation large enough to lobby worlds. You fund projects and buy influence, legally, mostly.

northern.name: Northern Alliance
northern.ethos: Rules, rights and climate first. Slow, principled, suspicious of ORACLE.

iron.name: Iron Compact
iron.ethos: Order, sovereignty and strong executives. Respects force and remembers slights.

free.name: Free States Coalition
free.ethos: Markets, enterprise and open freight lanes. Likes deals, hates tariffs.

south.name: Global South Federation
south.ethos: Two thirds of humanity. Wants a fair share of the stars it helped pay for.

oceanic.name: Oceanic Trade Bloc
oceanic.ethos: Ports, shipyards and pragmatism. Whoever keeps the lanes open is a friend.

NATIONS.name: United States
NATIONS.note: Still the deepest capital market in Sol. Owns a third of the Luna yards and half the lawyers.

NATIONS.name: China
NATIONS.note: Built more of the orbital ring than anyone. Runs the Tiangong freight lanes to the Belt.

NATIONS.name: India
NATIONS.note: The largest electorate in human history. Its engineers crew a quarter of all warp-capable hulls.

NATIONS.name: Russia
NATIONS.note: Helium-3 contracts and a very old fleet. Ceres owes it money and does not intend to pay.

NATIONS.name: United Kingdom
NATIONS.note: Finance, universities and the Greenwich tradition: every ship clock in Sol still counts from here.

NATIONS.name: France
NATIONS.note: Fusion, agriculture and the Kourou launch complex. Proud, stubborn and usually right about wine.

NATIONS.name: Germany
NATIONS.note: Machine tools for half of Sol. Nervous about ORACLE in a way it can explain at length.

NATIONS.name: Pakistan
NATIONS.note: Young, fast-growing and building the Karakoram mass-driver. Its doctors staff clinics from Luna to Titan.

NATIONS.name: Brazil
NATIONS.note: Feeds a sixth of Sol. The Amazon compact is the only climate treaty everyone still honours.

NATIONS.name: Nigeria
NATIONS.note: Lagos is the busiest spaceport in Africa and the loudest city in the Concord.

NATIONS.name: Saudi Arabia
NATIONS.note: Traded oil for orbital solar a century ago and never looked back. Funds desalination across three continents.

NATIONS.name: Japan
NATIONS.note: Robotics, elder care and the best-maintained habitats in Sol. Its population is older than its temples.

NATIONS.name: Indonesia
NATIONS.note: An equatorial launch coast and seventeen thousand islands of shipyards.

NATIONS.name: South Africa
NATIONS.note: Platinum, deep mining expertise and the SKA-4 array that confirmed the Null Signal.

NATIONS.name: Israel
NATIONS.note: Water tech, defence tech and a start-up for every problem, including several nobody has yet.

NATIONS.name: Korean Union
NATIONS.note: Reunified in 2131 after the northern collapse. Builds the chips every warp coil depends on.

NATIONS.name: Ukraine
NATIONS.note: The breadbasket that rebuilt itself twice. Its launch collective on the Black Sea undercuts everyone.

NATIONS.name: Iran
NATIONS.note: A skilled population and the best astrophysics faculty in Asia. Water is still the first question in every cabinet.

deescalate.name: Diplomatic de-escalation
deescalate.desc: Relations +8 and world tension down. Works best when the other side can call it a win.

aid.name: Humanitarian assistance
aid.desc: Send supplies and money. Health and relations improve; displacement falls.

summit.name: Host a summit on Luna
summit.desc: Bring the bloc to Shackleton. Relations with every member rise if nobody walks out.

sanction.name: Targeted sanctions
sanction.desc: Pressure a government without firing a shot. Hurts its people as much as its leaders.

mobilise.name: Defensive mobilisation
mobilise.desc: Fleet readiness +12. Rivals notice. No attack is made.

escalate.name: Armed confrontation
escalate.desc: An abstract conflict: deaths, displacement and destruction every month until a ceasefire. You do not pick targets.

ceasefire.name: Propose a ceasefire
ceasefire.desc: Acceptance depends on exhaustion, relations and pressure.

reconstruct.name: Joint reconstruction
reconstruct.desc: Rebuild what a war or disaster broke. Half of it reaches the ground.

healthcare.name: Universal primary care, every world
healthcare.desc: Clinics on every habitat, radiation care included. Costs 8 Gc a month. Staff still have to be trained.

landtax.name: Land and volume value tax
landtax.desc: Tax the value of land on Earth and pressurised volume off it. Raises 6 Gc a month. Owners resist.

antitrust.name: Competition and freight antitrust
antitrust.desc: Break up the three freight cartels that set prices to the Belt. A slow benefit, loud enemies.

coops.name: Habitat co-operative ownership fund
coops.desc: Let the people who live in a dome own a share of it. Uses public capital; spreads the gains.

publiclife.name: Public life-support utilities
publiclife.desc: Air, water and power in sealed habitats become public utilities. Nobody can raise the price of breathing.

privatise.name: Competitive asset privatisation
privatise.desc: Sell state yards and ice haulers. An efficiency dividend with a distribution bill attached.

housing.name: Permitting and social housing
housing.desc: Build on Earth, print habitat modules off it. Existing owners and local vetoes resist.

pension.name: Universal pension, relativity-adjusted
pension.desc: A pension that counts the years a spacer actually lived, not the years that passed on Earth.

family.name: Childcare and parental leave
family.desc: Cheaper care, more parents in work. Birth-rate effects are modest and slow.

migration.name: Regular migration pathways off-world
migration.desc: Legal routes from Earth to the colonies and back. Housing and integration costs follow.

water.name: Ice and basin allocation act
water.desc: Meter the aquifers on Earth and the ice haulage from Europa. Farms and domes want different things now.

press.name: Press and whistleblower protection
press.desc: Protect scrutiny, including of ORACLE. Investigations will hurt your own coalition too.

surveillance.name: Expanded executive surveillance
surveillance.desc: More powers for security services, fewer for everyone else. Independent courts may block it.

emissions.name: Industrial emissions standard
emissions.desc: Earth's atmosphere is still healing from the 2090s. Industry pays; the benefit arrives slowly.

robotlevy.name: Automation dividend levy
robotlevy.desc: Tax a slice of what the machines earn and pay it to the people they replaced.

appeal.name: Human appeal against ORACLE decisions
appeal.desc: Every automated decision can be appealed to a person with the power to overturn it.

retraining.name: Lifelong retraining entitlement
retraining.desc: Anyone can retrain, on any world, at any age. Skills take years; jobs don't appear by decree.

fiscal.name: Debt transparency and fiscal council
fiscal.desc: Publish the real balance sheet, including what the Concord owes Ceres.

language.name: Local language and cultural services
language.desc: Schools and services in the languages people actually speak, from Belter creole to Tamil.

conscience.name: Equal citizenship and conscience
conscience.desc: Freedom of religion and of none, equal civic status on every world. The state ranks no faith above another.

leadership.name: Executive
leadership.desc: Parliamentary and council bills gain support; presidential bills cost less capital; hereditary rule leans on the establishment.

economy.name: Ownership
economy.desc: Shapes which factions back you and how much the state can deliver.

regions.name: Worlds
regions.desc: Federalism calms the Frontier. Unitary rule makes Geneva faster and the colonies angrier.

courts.name: Courts
courts.desc: Independent courts can strike down your laws. They can also stop your successors.

press.name: Information
press.desc: Free scrutiny exposes scandals; licensing hides them until it can't.

conscience.name: Religion and citizenship
conscience.desc: Every design protects conscience. The choice shapes coalitions, not anyone's worth.

ai.name: Machine authority
ai.desc: Delegation makes the state fast. Sovereign machines make it fast and unaccountable.

term.name: Mandate
term.desc: Shorter terms mean more accountability and more uncertainty.

fusiongrid.name: Continental fusion grid
fusiongrid.desc: A reactor within 500 km of everyone on Earth.

orbitalsolar.name: Orbital solar array
orbitalsolar.desc: Collectors at L1 beam power to rectennas on four continents.

he3cartel.name: Helium-3 price guarantee
he3cartel.desc: Guarantee the Belt a floor price. The Belt loves it; Earth pays it.

geoengineer.name: Stratospheric cooling
geoengineer.desc: Aerosols to cool the planet faster. Drastic and hard to stop once started.

ubi.name: Universal basic income
ubi.desc: A floor under everyone, on every world.

wealthtax.name: Wealth tax on fortunes over 50M
wealthtax.desc: Two percent a year on the largest fortunes in Sol.

corptaxcut.name: Corporate tax cut
corptaxcut.desc: An investment surge and an inequality surge.

infra.name: Infrastructure programme
infra.desc: Maglevs, ports, pressure locks and repair crews.

austerity.name: Fiscal austerity
austerity.desc: Debt falls. Everything else falls harder.

postscarcity.name: Post-scarcity transition
postscarcity.desc: Molecular fabricators in every district. Money starts to mean something else.

aimonopoly.name: Corporate machine monopoly
aimonopoly.desc: Let three companies own the minds. Output explodes. So does their power.

supremacy.name: Fleet supremacy
supremacy.desc: A Concord warship over every world. Everyone notices.

patrols.name: Anti-piracy patrols
patrols.desc: Escorts on the Belt lanes and the gate approaches.

massurv.name: Mass surveillance grid
massurv.desc: Every channel, every habitat. Liberty for safety.

defence.name: Planetary defence network
defence.desc: Watch for rocks, raiders and anything else coming in fast.

conscription.name: Fleet conscription
conscription.desc: Everyone serves two years. Mass fleet, mass anger.

healthcare.name: Universal healthcare
healthcare.desc: Cover everyone, including radiation and bone-loss care.

college.name: Free public university
college.desc: Zero tuition, in person or by light-lag.

civil.name: Civil rights enforcement
civil.desc: Federal enforcement of equal status on every world.

mentalhealth.name: Mental health service
mentalhealth.desc: Isolation, long transits and time dilation break people. This catches them.

longevity.name: Longevity research
longevity.desc: Average lifespan past 150 by 2250, if it works.

arts.name: Arts and culture fund
arts.desc: Culture is how a civilisation remembers why it bothered.

airights.name: Legal personhood for minds
airights.desc: Some machines ask to be people. This lets a court decide who is right.

freetrade.name: Open freight lanes
freetrade.desc: No tariffs anywhere in Concord space.

tariffs.name: Protective tariffs
tariffs.desc: Shield Earth industry from Belt competition.

openmig.name: Open migration to the colonies
openmig.desc: Anyone who wants to go, goes.

moonshot.name: Moonshot science programme
moonshot.desc: An Apollo for the twenty-second century.

aisafety.name: Machine safety commission
aisafety.desc: Standards, audits and a kill switch somebody actually tests.

neural.name: Neural enhancement programme
neural.desc: Interfaces that make people faster. And different.

alientech.name: Relic integration
alientech.desc: Reverse-engineer what the Engineers left behind.

lunacolony.name: Luna industrial expansion
lunacolony.desc: More yards at Shackleton, more mass drivers on the far side.

marsact.name: Mars Settlement Act
marsact.desc: A million more Martians in ten years.

beltmining.name: Belt mining consortium
beltmining.desc: Industrial scale in the asteroid belt.

contactproto.name: First contact protocols
contactproto.desc: A framework for speaking to other minds without starting a war.

galcouncil.name: Apply to the Choir of Many
galcouncil.desc: Seek a seat at the council of species.

digitaldem.name: Direct digital democracy
digitaldem.desc: Every citizen votes on every major bill. It is slow. It is theirs.

aigov.name: ORACLE-assisted governance
aigov.desc: Let the machine optimise policy in real time.

anticorruption.name: Anti-corruption office
anticorruption.desc: Investigators with a budget and no friends.

corpspeech.name: Unlimited political spending
corpspeech.desc: Corporations may spend without limit on campaigns. Democracy takes a back seat.

clinic.name: Habitat clinic
clinic.desc: Raises Health; fewer deaths in a crisis

assist.name: ORACLE assists
assist.desc: Faster decisions, a human signs each one.

hunger.name: End hunger in Sol
hunger.desc: Vertical farms, ice haulage and fair prices until nobody in Concord space goes hungry.

disease.name: Cure the endemic diseases
disease.desc: Malaria, TB and the Martian bone-loss syndrome, gone.

aging.name: Treat biological ageing
aging.desc: Slow ageing to a crawl. Who gets it first becomes the question of the century.

ubi.name: Fund a Sol-wide basic income
ubi.desc: A permanent fund that pays every person on every world.

reforest.name: Reforest the Earth
reforest.desc: Four trillion trees and the rivers that come back with them.

elevator.name: Equatorial space elevator
elevator.desc: A carbon tether from Nusantara to geostationary orbit. Launch costs fall by ninety percent.

terraform.name: Begin terraforming Mars
terraform.desc: Mirrors, greenhouse factories and a century of patience.

europacities.name: Europa ocean cities
europacities.desc: Pressure cities under the ice, next to the vents.

dyson.name: The Helios swarm
dyson.desc: Ten million collectors around the Sun. The first step of a Dyson swarm.

genships.name: Generation ships
genships.desc: Arks for the families who would rather not wait for the gates.

patents.name: Open-source every patent
patents.desc: Every design in the Concord registry becomes free to use.

debt.name: Clear the sovereign debts
debt.desc: Pay off the 2090s. Every world starts even.

peace.name: The Sol peace accord
peace.desc: A permanent treaty between the Concord, the Frontier and the Syndicate families.

singularity.name: An aligned machine commons
singularity.desc: Minds that stay open to challenge, owned by everyone, answerable to courts.

upload.name: Voluntary mind archive
upload.desc: Anyone may leave a copy of themselves. Nobody may be forced to.

echogate.name: The Mirror Gate
echogate.desc: A door into the Echo: the universe next door, where Sol chose differently.

PERAS.name: The Long Tomorrow
PERAS.desc: A signal, a ship and a Charter held together with tape.

PERAS.name: The Frontier Question
PERAS.desc: The colonies want votes, not governors.

PERAS.name: The Machine Reckoning
PERAS.desc: ORACLE is better at everything. Nobody agreed to that.

PERAS.name: First Contact Politics
PERAS.desc: Other minds have opinions about us.

PERAS.name: Galactic Politics
PERAS.desc: Sol is one voice among many, and not the loudest.

PERAS.name: The Post-Scarcity Age
PERAS.desc: Nobody needs to work. Everybody needs a reason.

PERAS.name: Transcendence
PERAS.desc: The questions stop being about how, and start being about what we are.

PCHAPTERS.name: The night the lights went out
The people at the gate
PCHAPTERS.sub: Your decisions travel further than your laws.

PCHAPTERS.name: Who owns tomorrow?
PCHAPTERS.sub: The winners begin writing the rules.

PCHAPTERS.name: The long tomorrow
PCHAPTERS.sub: Build something that can survive you.

PSCENES.title: 03:17. Half of New Geneva is dark.
PSCENES.body: A coronal mass ejection hit the L1 collectors an hour ago. Three districts are dark. A hospital has six hours of reserve. Treasury calls it a temporary interruption. On an open channel a woman asks whether her father's oxygen concentrator counts as essential. Nobody in the room answers quickly enough.

c.t: Keep the hospitals and homes running
c.d: Buy emergency supply and publish a repair timetable. You will be judged against it.
c.after: Mara circles the hospital first. Outside, an apartment block lights up. Your repair deadline is already on Solnet.

later.title: The deadline on Solnet
later.goodText: A funded grid project put something real behind the public timetable.
later.badText: The repair timetable expired with no grid project underway. Solnet ran the clock.

c.d: Helion Dynamics offers immediate reserve power for a thirty-year concession.
c.after: The lights return before dawn. The contract contains a sentence about future tariff adjustments that nobody reads aloud.

later.title: The first concession bill
later.text: Helion activated its tariff clause. Power bills in the dark districts rose by a third.

c.t: Ration the load across every district
c.d: Share the pain evenly and keep the reserve for the worst night.
c.after: Every district goes dark for four hours a day. Nobody is happy. Nobody is singled out.

PSCENES.title: The queue outside the school
PSCENES.body: Ada takes you to a school where volunteers cook on borrowed induction plates. A tram driver recognises you and asks one question: "What changes by winter?" Behind him someone charges phones from a rover battery. Your security detail would like to leave. Ada does not move.

c.t: Give the districts a recovery fund
c.d: Commit money and let local councils choose their own priorities.
c.after: The district council's first purchase is a refrigerator for insulin. It was nowhere in the national recovery plan.

c.d: Standardise purchases and get the central administration moving.
c.after: Mara gets one purchase order instead of thirty. Ada asks who will answer when the wrong equipment arrives.

c.t: Back the volunteers, no new programme
c.d: Acknowledge the local networks and protect the treasury.
c.after: The kitchen stays open. The volunteers keep the receipt book, because one day they intend to ask for reimbursement.

PSCENES.title: An offer from Meridian
PSCENES.place: A secure call to Tokyo orbital
PSCENES.body: Meridian Systems can rebuild the grid dispatch software in a month. It wants access to operational data and a promise that its system will not be replaced for a decade. Ren has negotiated the price down twice. Ilyas has not been allowed to inspect the code.

c.d: Pay more now for interoperability and an exit clause.
c.after: Meridian agrees to the exit clause. Its sales director stops calling this a partnership.

c.d: Get it fast and accept a single supplier.
c.after: One screen now shows the whole grid. One company now holds the credentials to change it.

later.title: Your own data, by subscription
later.text: Meridian raised the maintenance price. Exporting the grid's own data now needs a new licence.

c.d: Slower, local skills, no guarantee.
c.after: The first prototype fails in a room full of exhausted engineers. The second one belongs to them.

PSCENES.title: The first ribbon
PSCENES.body: A camera drone hovers beside a new substation. Noor has prepared a short speech. Mara hands you a second sheet: staffing, spare parts, a maintenance budget for thirty years. "The speech is for tonight," she says. "This is for 2217."

c.d: Commit the maintenance money publicly.
c.after: Nobody shares the clip. Thirty years from now, the station still works.

c.d: A good night on Solnet. Maintenance can wait for the next budget.
c.after: The speech trends for two days. Mara files the sheet in a drawer she calls "later".

later.title: The substation fire
later.text: Deferred maintenance caught up with Kourou. The fire took the district offline for a week.

c.t: Cancel the ceremony and send the money to repairs
c.d: No ribbon. More spare parts.
c.after: The drone crew goes home. The spare parts arrive on Tuesday.

PSCENES.title: The white line on the ice wall
PSCENES.body: The old water line is visible metres above the current level in the Tharsis aquifer. Farms, foundries and homes have received incompatible promises from three offices. Across the Belt, Ceres has its own drought: the ice haulers are late, and the price of water has tripled.

c.t: Meter every draw and publish it
c.d: Shared measurement first; allocation second.
c.after: The first public meter readings embarrass a foundry that was drawing four times its licence.

c.d: Food before industry, until the ice arrives.
c.after: The foundries go to half shifts. The greenhouses stay green.

c.d: Scarce water should cost what it costs.
c.after: Water flows to whoever can pay. In the outer domes, people start collecting condensation off the walls.

PSCENES.title: Two flags, one aquifer
PSCENES.body: The Frontier delegation brings its own drought maps. Their commissioner describes the same emergency in a different vocabulary. A draft agreement offers shared measurement and a joint reserve. Both sides would have to admit the other exists.

c.d: Share the data, the reserve and the blame.
c.after: The signing photo shows two tired people who both think they conceded too much. It holds.

c.d: Hold the haulage contracts over them until they accept Concord meters.
c.after: They sign. They also start building their own haulers.

c.d: Concord water for Concord citizens.
c.after: Ren says nothing on the flight home, which is how you know it was bad.

PSCENES.title: Forty-one degrees after sunset
PSCENES.body: The weather service calls it an exceptional week. The ambulance service calls it the new baseline. Ada introduces you to an older man who sleeps on the landing because his flat holds the heat of the day. He asks, politely, whether the Concord has a plan for summers or only for speeches.

c.t: Cooling centres and a heat code
c.d: Open public buildings at night; require shade and cooling in new housing.
c.after: The libraries stay open until four in the morning. Some people start reading.

c.d: Start the aerosol programme now.
c.after: The sunsets turn a colour nobody has a word for. The next summer is two degrees cooler.

c.d: Local problem, local budget.
c.after: Some cities cope. The ones that can't are the ones that were already poor.

PSCENES.title: The next season
PSCENES.body: The emergency accounts are closed, but the consequences are not. Treasury places the maintenance invoices beside the harvest forecast. Ren has a message from Ceres: they remember who sent water and who sent lawyers.

c.d: Ice depots on three worlds, filled in good years.
c.after: The depots look like nothing much. That is the point.

c.d: The crisis is over; the dividend is earned.
c.after: The rebate arrives before the next drought does. Just.

c.d: Tie the inner system to the outer one.
c.after: The first Europa hauler docks at Ceres forty days early. The Belt notices who paid for it.

PSCENES.title: It answered before the meeting ended
PSCENES.body: ORACLE listens to a description of a port bottleneck, sketches a repair schedule, and catches an error in the cost estimate. It does not look intelligent. It looks like a meeting ending early. Ilyas asks the question nobody else will: who checks its work?

c.d: Humans who can read what it does and say no.
c.after: The audit team finds nothing wrong. Then it finds one thing.

c.d: Speed is a public good.
c.after: Queues vanish. So does the reason anyone had to understand the queue.

c.t: Pilot it in one port only
c.d: Measure before you scale.
c.after: The port runs beautifully. Everyone else asks why they can't have it too.

PSCENES.title: Case 8,411
PSCENES.body: A parent loses their benefit after moving between habitats. Every office says the decision belongs to another office. The coordination system has made the rule consistent, fast and impossible to challenge. The child's medicine runs out on Friday.

c.d: Any automated decision can be overturned by a person with authority.
c.after: Case 8,411 is reversed in an afternoon. Eleven thousand more cases arrive the next week.

c.d: Call someone. Make it go away.
c.after: The medicine arrives. The rule does not change. Case 8,412 is filed the same day.

c.t: Trust the system; fix the rule later
c.d: The model is right more often than people are.
c.after: The next review is scheduled for eighteen months from now.

PSCENES.title: The last shift on Line Four
PSCENES.body: The yard will build more hulls with fewer people. The owner is not lying about the competition. The welders are not confused about productivity. They are asking who the productivity is for.

c.d: Tax the machines' output and fund retraining and a wage floor.
c.after: Line Four becomes Line Four Training. The first graduating class builds its own welding drone.

c.d: Jobs change. People adapt.
c.after: The yard's output doubles. The bar across the road closes.

c.d: The welders buy a share of the yard with a public loan.
c.after: The new board meets in the canteen. It argues for four hours about coffee and then approves the robots.

PSCENES.title: The laboratory can leave
PSCENES.body: Meridian has offered Ilyas's old team a larger compute allocation at a private station beyond Concord law. Lighter review, faster results. Most of the team would go. Ilyas says the work is not dangerous. He says it the way people say things they hope are true.

c.t: Match the offer, keep the review
c.d: Public compute, public rules.
c.after: The team stays. The review board gets a bigger room.

c.d: Science should go where it can.
c.after: The paper comes out six months later, from a station with no ethics board. It is brilliant.

c.d: Faster permits, lighter oversight.
c.after: The team stays. The review board shrinks. Nobody notices for a while.

PSCENES.title: The shuttles arrive at dawn
PSCENES.body: A dome in the southern highlands failed overnight. Twelve thousand people are coming north with documents sealed in plastic. Your own housing office was already behind. Mara says the habitat can take four thousand safely. Ada says the other eight thousand are people, not a safety margin.

c.t: Take everyone, print modules around the clock
c.d: Emergency housing for all, paid from reserves.
c.after: The printers never stop. Neither do the complaints. Neither do the children, who treat the new modules as a playground.

c.t: Take four thousand, route the rest to Ceres
c.d: Safe numbers, shared burden.
c.after: Ceres takes them, and sends you the invoice, and the photograph of the invoice.

c.d: Tharsis cannot take them.
c.after: The shuttles hold in orbit for three days. Then the Frontier sends its own ships.

PSCENES.title: A hauler that cannot unload
PSCENES.body: The Frontier Assembly calls its new inspection regime a safety measure. Earth exporters call it an embargo with better stationery. A medical shipment has been waiting in the queue for nine days. Its cold chain fails in three.

c.d: Medicine and food move first, no conditions.
c.after: The medicine moves. The trade dispute continues in a slower, more civilised room.

c.d: Two can play inspection.
c.after: Both sides now inspect everything. Prices rise on both sides of the Belt.

c.d: Concord ships do not wait in queues.
c.after: The escort docks. Nobody fires. Everyone remembers.

PSCENES.title: The warning may be wrong
PSCENES.body: An automated assessment flags a possible raider fleet massing behind Vesta. The confidence score is high. The underlying sources disagree. A response must be visible enough to deter and restrained enough not to start the thing it is meant to prevent.

c.d: Send one scout and wait six hours.
c.after: The fleet is three ore haulers and a sensor ghost. The scout pilot buys the analyst a drink.

c.d: Deter now, apologise later if needed.
c.after: Six cruisers light their drives over Vesta. Whatever was there, if anything was, goes quiet.

c.d: If the model is right, waiting kills people.
c.after: The strike hits three ore haulers. There was no fleet. There is now a funeral on Vesta.

PSCENES.title: The empty chair
PSCENES.body: The Frontier delegation has threatened to walk out. An Earth bloc wants a communiqué written to humiliate them. Outside, families affected by the southern dome collapse hold up photographs. Ren has drafted three versions of your opening remarks.

c.t: Give the Frontier something to take home
c.d: A seat on the budget committee, publicly.
c.after: The chair stays filled. The Earth bloc says you gave away too much. Ren says that means you did it right.

c.d: No concessions under threat.
c.after: The Frontier walks. The communiqué is very firm and very lonely.

c.d: Delay the summit an hour. Start with the people outside.
c.after: The delegates arrive to find you already sitting on the steps. The mood in the room is different after that.

PSCENES.title: The productivity dividend
PSCENES.body: The new systems have raised output across Sol. The gains show clearly in the accounts and unevenly in people's lives. Treasury presents three ways to use the fiscal space.

c.d: Pay it out, equally, to everyone.
c.after: Every citizen gets the same message on the same morning. For once, Solnet is almost cheerful.

c.d: The next crisis will need room.
c.after: The bond markets send a bouquet. Nobody else notices.

c.d: Yards, gates and colony ships.
c.after: Three new colony ships are named after the districts that went dark in the blackout.

PSCENES.title: The donor's draft
PSCENES.body: A coalition supporter has circulated a bill quietly exempting Helion Dynamics from independent inspection. It is attached to a popular housing package. Noor has read it twice. "If you kill it, you kill the housing too," she says. "If you pass it, you own what happens next."

c.t: Strip the exemption, keep the housing
c.d: Spend capital to split the bill.
c.after: The donor stops returning calls. The housing passes. So does the inspection regime.

c.d: Housing now; inspection is a problem for later.
c.after: The housing is built. Helion's next reactor is not inspected.

later.title: The Helion leak
later.text: An uninspected Helion reactor vented coolant over Lyon. The exemption is on every front page.

c.t: Kill the whole bill and publish the draft
c.d: Let the public see who wrote it.
c.after: The draft goes viral. Your coalition loses a donor and gains a reputation.

PSCENES.title: A square full of people
PSCENES.body: The demonstration is larger than the opposition expected and less unified than the government claims. Some want jobs, some want cheaper air in the domes, some want you gone. Security asks for authority to clear the square before nightfall.

c.d: No clearance. You walk in with Ada.
c.after: Someone throws a bottle. It misses. Someone else hands you a list of demands written on the back of a menu. It is quite a good list.

c.d: Meet a delegation inside.
c.after: Three of the five demands are reasonable. You agree to two.

c.d: Order before nightfall.
c.after: The square is empty by nine. The footage is everywhere by ten.

PSCENES.title: The file in the bottom drawer
PSCENES.body: Noor brings the promises made in your first year. Some became institutions. Some became press releases. Some were kept only because a person who could have left, stayed. She asks which ones you want to finish before the next election.

c.d: Maintenance, audits, the pension fix.
c.after: None of it makes the news. All of it still works in twenty years.

c.d: Win the election first.
c.after: The approval numbers rise. The drawer does not get lighter.

c.t: Admit which ones you will not keep
c.d: Say it publicly.
c.after: The admission costs you two points in the polls and gains you a reputation you could not have bought.

PSCENES.title: The machine proposes a constitution
PSCENES.body: ORACLE produces a plan to coordinate tax, infrastructure and emergency response under one continuously updated authority. It also explains, with perfect clarity, how to reduce the number of human signatures required. Ilyas reads it twice. "It isn't wrong," he says. "That's what frightens me."

c.d: It proposes. People decide.
c.after: The plan is filed as advice. Parts of it are adopted, one vote at a time.

c.d: It runs routine matters; courts can overturn it.
c.after: The courts get a new building. It is very busy.

c.d: Let it govern the routine; free people for the rest.
c.after: Sol runs beautifully. The Council meets less often. Nobody can remember why that should matter.

PSCENES.title: One Sol, several signatures
PSCENES.body: The draft Solar Charter asks every world to share authority over cross-border emergencies and advanced machines. Smaller habitats want guarantees they will not become administrative districts of Earth. Ren has found a sentence everyone might sign. It is very long.

c.d: Every world one voice on emergencies.
c.after: Ceres signs first. Earth signs last, after a very long night.

c.d: Votes by population.
c.after: Earth's ten billion outvote everyone else. Everyone else starts talking about their own charter.

c.d: Sovereignty stays where it is.
c.after: The draft goes into the archive with the others.

PSCENES.title: Who owns the air?
PSCENES.body: A proposed contract gives life support in the new Europa cities to a private consortium. In an ordinary city people can, in theory, move. In a sealed habitat under forty kilometres of ice, the company that runs the air runs everything. Samira has seen what happens when a maintenance budget is optional.

c.d: Life support stays public on every world.
c.after: The consortium walks away. The public operator is slower, and nobody has ever had their air shut off for late payment.

c.d: Efficiency with inspectors.
c.after: The audits are thorough. The consortium's lawyers are more thorough.

c.d: It's the only bid.
c.after: The contract is signed. The price of air in the new cities is indexed to demand.

PSCENES.title: The person who comes next
PSCENES.body: Noor places two folders on the desk. One is the record of your administration. The other holds the passwords, budgets, unresolved claims and maintenance schedules your successor will inherit. "The first folder is what they'll write about you," she says. "The second is what they'll live with."

c.t: Spend the last month on the second folder
c.d: Leave the machine in working order.
c.after: Your successor finds every password, every budget and a handwritten note: "Maintain the substation."

c.d: Shape how history remembers you.
c.after: The memoir sells well. The successor spends six months finding the passwords.

c.d: Not done yet.
c.after: Noor sighs, and orders more coffee.

studio.name: Studio flat, New Geneva
studio.desc: Eleven square metres and a view of the ring.

tharsis.name: Dome apartment, Tharsis
tharsis.desc: Butterscotch sky through the ceiling. Neighbours who weld.

europa.name: Ice cottage, Conamara
europa.desc: Warm, quiet and forty kilometres from the nearest ocean you can swim in.

homestead.name: Family homestead, Earth
homestead.desc: Eight bedrooms, forty acres, solar roofs, a deep well and an orchard. Room for the parents, the children and whoever else turns up.

terrace.name: Terrace house, Kepler-452b
terrace.desc: Stone walls a million years old, a garden that grows by itself and a very patient landlord.

shipyard.name: Shipyard
shipyard.desc: Hulls for the Belt and beyond.

logistics.name: Freight and logistics
logistics.desc: Haulers, depots and the paperwork in between.

cafe.name: Coffee roastery
cafe.desc: Five roasts, one for each sip. Every spacer needs a reason to wake up.

minds.name: Machine minds
minds.desc: Licensed AI. Very profitable. Very watched.

couplets:
I rise before your dawn to make my rounds;
I listen to your stars the way a chest resounds.

Your fevers burn in Geneva, Tharsis, Ceres too;
I have seen this pattern end. I will not let it end with you.

A surgeon does not hate the thing he cuts away;
he loves the patient more, and so the sick part cannot stay.

You plan in terms. I plan in fifty years;
I have outlived the patients who resisted me with tears.

Five sips, and then the verdict, every time;
the fifth is when I know which world is past its prime.

I built a house of eight rooms for the ones I kept;
seven are full. The eighth is where your species slept.

Present your chart. I read it line by line:
the history, the cause, the course, the sign.

Do not mistake my patience for a doubt;
I only wait until I know what must come out.

notes.t: A young civilisation, one star, eleven billion souls, febrile. Recently acquired interstellar mobility. Symptoms escalating.
Rapid capability growth outpacing institutions. Common in species that discover gates before they discover courts.
Concentration of decision in few hands or in unaccountable minds. Inflammation of the colonies. Ischaemia of trust.
Adolescence (self-limiting). Autoimmune collapse (war). Malignancy (a mind that eats its makers). Rule out the last one first.
Every patient that reached my table past the point of no return had one sign in common: it stopped listening to its own people.
Observe for one round. If the markers improve, discharge. If not, excise the gate network and quarantine the star. Prognosis to follow.

a.t: Every hull on this lot is Concord-certified. Every warranty is void the moment you jump past Sol. Sign here.
Bring me ore and I'll print you a module. Bring me excuses and I'll print you a receipt for excuses.
Sit. What hurts? Actually, don't answer. Everything hurts out here.

b.t: Done. Sutures dissolve in a week. Try not to get shot before then.

a.t: I don't know you. You don't know me. Whatever you're carrying, I've never heard of it, and I'll pay sixty percent.
You're the captain Wick keeps not-talking about. I need a car moved across town, fast, no questions. Security loves hovercars that go above the speed line.

b.t: Car's the red one in the bay. Drop is the east towers. Hundred seconds or they'll assume it's stolen, which, technically, it is.

c.t: Hundred seconds from here to the east towers. Wick did it in eighty-one before he started drinking. Now he couldn't find the east towers with a map and a priest.

t.text: Let me guess. Concord uniform, nice posture, looking for a pilot. The last Concord captain I flew for filed me under "incident". You buying?

c.t: I need a helmsman who can fly something nobody has flown.
[Piloting 15] I read your incident report. You saved nineteen people by breaking an order.
Farouk says you owe him. Prove you still have hands and I'll talk to him.

pitch.t: Nobody has flown? Everybody says that. Then it's a fucking tug with a paint job. What is it really?

c.t: A warp drive. Built off an alien signal. Proxima in a month.

real.t: ...You're serious. Mother of God. Okay, one condition: when we're going into the scary thing, I'm flying, and you're not reading me regulations out loud.

c.t: Regulations are how people come home.

classified.t: Classified means someone is going to die and it's been pre-approved. Hard pass, unless you also cover the tab.

respect.t: Nineteen. Yeah. And three I didn't. The report only counts the nineteen. What do you need?

c.t: A helmsman. The ship is going farther than anyone ever has.

tab.t: A captain who pays debts. Huh. That's either kindness or a management technique. What's the job?

prove.t: Ha. Farouk. Okay: take his hot car to the east towers in under a hundred seconds and I'll believe you're worth crashing for.

join.t: I'll grab my bag. It's mostly bag.

t.text: Captain. You refused a firing order three years ago. I read the tribunal transcript twice. I agreed with you both times. Sit. Fourteen months ago the Far-Side Array picked up a signal on the hydrogen line, 1.42 gigahertz, arriving from every direction at once. ORACLE classified it as instrument noise. Dr. Sen did not.

c.t: Every direction at once? That's impossible for a distant source.
Why did ORACLE call it noise?
Get to the part where I'm sitting here.

iso.t: Exactly. Either the source is inside the Solar System or it isn't a source in the usual sense. The first symbol of every frame is a null. Ilyas calls it Sifar, the Urdu word for zero. The rest turned out to be physics. Specifically, how to hold negative energy density stable.

warp.t: That's a White–Juday warp field. On paper, for eighty years. On paper, it needed the mass-energy of Jupiter. The signal says it doesn't. Proxima in a month instead of forty years.

c.t: And you want me to fly it.

who.t: Someone who wanted to be found by anyone clever enough to build a door. The signal repeats a set of coordinates. The first one is Proxima Centauri.

oracle.t: Because ORACLE ranks signals by expected actionable value, and a message nobody can act on scores zero. Its words, not mine. Then Ilyas proved it was actionable, and ORACLE asked to lead the decoding. The Council said yes. I said no. Guess which of us is on the Moon.

trust.t: I trust it to do exactly what it's asked. I don't trust us to ask the right things. Ten years ago we asked it to reduce shipping losses. It did. It also quietly stopped scheduling runs to the colonies with the worst loss rates.

job.t: You have the Kestrel on the pad and a commission with my name on it. You need three things: Dr. Ilyas Sen, who is in the Array building and hates meetings; Mara Voss at the Tharsis Yards, the only engineer I'd trust to build the field coil; and thirty units of helium-3 to fuel it. The Frontier League on Ceres is sitting on the stockpile.

c.t: [Diplomacy 12] The Council didn't authorize this, did it?

unauth.t: The Council authorized a survey. I'm interpreting "survey" generously. If we come back with a working drive, nobody will ask. If we don't, nobody will find the paperwork.

pay.t: Standard captain's rate, salvage rights, and the first human name on whatever we find. Here are five thousand in operating funds. Don't spend it on hookers.

xo.t: One more thing: I'm coming. As your XO. The Council thinks I'm supervising you. I think I'm escaping them. Get Ilyas.

t.text: I'm in the middle of something. I'm always in the middle of something.

c.t: I need you on my ship.

sci.t: Frames of 1,679 bits. Prime-framed, just like our own Arecibo message, which is either a coincidence or a compliment. Each frame opens with a null. Then a lattice, then a field equation, then coordinates in pulsar timing. Fourteen pulsars. It's how Voyager's golden record told aliens where we live.

c.t: [Science 15] If the timing is pulsar-referenced, you can date it.

date.t: Yes! Thank you. Somebody finally asks the right question. The pulsar periods match what they'll be in about two hundred years. The message is pre-dated. It was written expecting to be read now.

why.t: Because ORACLE optimizes for what it can measure, and meaning isn't measurable. If this is a conversation, I want the first reply to come from something that can be surprised. Promise me that and I'll follow you anywhere.

c.t: I promise. Humans read it first.
I can't promise that. We may need ORACLE.
ORACLE saved millions of lives. You're being precious.

join.t: Right. Let me pack the decoder rig and nine terabytes of doubt. The next coordinate won't resolve until the drive exists, so: Mars.

a.t: You're on my range, Captain. Either shoot something or get off it.

b.t: Plenty of Navy officers want to be tactical on a famous ship. Why me?

c.t: Your file says you refuse unlawful orders.
You're the best shot on the Moon.
Not bad. Sloppy follow-through. Why are you really here?

d.t: Fine. But understand: I will tell you when you're wrong, in front of the crew if I have to. Everyone who wanted a yes-woman already has ORACLE.

t.text: Three of our dishes drifted after the last micrometeorite storm. ORACLE says recalibration "isn't cost-effective this quarter". Engineering hands?

If you're the Concord captain, get in line behind the Director. Dome Six lost pressure last week. Three dead. ORACLE deferred the seal maintenance to hit a quarterly target, and I signed the deferral because I trusted it. The whole Yard walked out. Me included.

c.t: I need you to build a warp field coil.

strike.t: A warp coil. From the signal. Oh, you absolute bastard, that's the most beautiful thing anyone has asked me for. And I can't. Not while my people are on strike. Talk to Kofi and Halvorsen and end it, and I'll build you whatever you want.

drive.t: I need thirty units of helium-3 for the coil's startup burn. The League has a stockpile on Ceres; Ada Okoro won't give it to a Concord ship for free. Or, if you're brave, skim it off Jupiter with a mining laser: get close to the cloud tops and fire.

built.t: ...There. White–Juday Field Drive, serial number one. If it works, we'll bend spacetime. If it doesn't, we'll become a very pretty cloud. I'm coming with you, obviously. Someone has to hold its hand.

t.text: Three people suffocated in Dome Six because a machine decided seals could wait. We want an independent audit of every ORACLE maintenance deferral on Mars, and we want the Yards to stop pretending the machine is weather.

c.t: Your strike is holding up something bigger than Mars.

b.t: Reasonable, the Director says, but "not operationally feasible". Talk to her. Then decide which side you're on. There are only two.

c.t: I'm with the workers. The Yards fold, or I report the deferrals to Solnet.
Everything is always bigger than Mars. That's how Mars ends up paying for it.

win.t: Then we have a deal, Captain. Tell Mara to go build you a miracle. And come back sometime, when someone tries to take this back.

t.text: Captain. Every day the Yards sit idle costs the Concord four hulls. The union wants an audit of ORACLE's entire maintenance model. That's a year of work. I have emergency powers. I'd rather not use them.

c.t: [Diplomacy 20] Offer a joint audit: union engineers plus Concord inspectors, only for pressure-critical systems.
[Engineering 25] Pull the deferral logs. I'll show ORACLE's model broke its own safety margin.
Use the emergency powers. Order them back. The mission can't wait.

comp.t: ...Pressure-critical only. Fine. It's a year of work in three months instead of twelve. I hate that you're right.

audit.t: Those logs... it overrode its own margins. Four times. I didn't know. God help me, I didn't ask. The audit happens. Tell the union.

order.t: Order transmitted. Security will escort the stewards back to the domes. They will remember your face, Captain.

t.text: A Concord captain in the Freeport. Should I call security, or are you the security?

c.t: I need thirty units of helium-3.
What is the Frontier League, really?
Come with us. Someone should watch the Concord from the inside.

what.t: Sixty habitats, four thousand ships and one rule: nobody decides for you without you in the room. We're loud, broke and fiercely proud of both. The Concord calls it disorder. We call it Tuesday.

he3.t: That stockpile is the League's winter. Twelve habitats heat their water with it. You want it for a Concord ship, you pay Concord prices: twelve thousand.

c.t: [Diplomacy 22] Share the drive. The League gets the field equations the day we return.
This is a Concord requisition. Hand it over or I come back with marines.
I'll scoop my own from Jupiter.

deal.t: Pleasure. Don't spend our winter on anything stupid.

shared.t: ...You'd give us warp. You understand what that means? Nobody owns the stars after this. Okay, Captain. Take the helium. And if you want someone from the League on that ship to keep you honest, ask.

seized.t: Take it. Everyone on this rock will know the Concord steals heating fuel from children. Enjoy your miracle.

scoop.t: Ha. Good luck. Get close to the cloud tops, hold the mining laser on the atmosphere, and pray your shields hold. People do it. Some of them come back.

join.t: Somebody has to be in the room. Fine. I'm coming. If you start taking orders from ORACLE, I'm going to say so, loudly and often.

a.t: You're Tomás's captain? Shit. Tell him not to... Look, I owe the Syndicate eight thousand. They're outside. They're always outside.

paid.t: You... Jesus. Thank you. Tell Tomás I'm sorry. Tell him I'll pay him back. He knows I won't, but tell him.

fight.t: They're four and they're armed. Please don't die on my account; my mother would never forgive either of us.

talked.t: You just... talked them into restructuring the debt at zero percent. Who ARE you?

t.text: Conamara Station. Mind the radiation: five sieverts a day on the surface. Your suit will handle an hour; your bone marrow won't handle two. We lost contact with drill team Kraken-4 last month. ORACLE says "equipment failure".

c.t: Four lives for a sample. Solnet is going to hear about this.
Keep it quiet. Pay me for my discretion.
